channel.title: Block Club Chicago - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Block Club Chicago (blockclubchicago.org)

item.title: Chicago’s Violence Interrupters Hail Drops In Gun Violence, Call For Steadier Funding
item.description: Advocates say establishing community violence intervention as a legitimate profession has been a key factor in Chicago's years-long decreases in shootings and homicides.

item.title: Waymo Starts Testing Self-Driving Cars In Chicago — But With Drivers, For Now
item.description: The self-driving cars, staged in a Downtown parking lot Tuesday, will hit the roads with the help of drivers Wednesday for "mapping and early data collection," a Waymo spokesperson said.

item.title: Wrigley Field To Host First-Ever Chicago HBCU Baseball Classic
item.description: Two historically Black universities, Prairie View A&M and Alabama A&M, will face off May 2 after a Cubs game at the only existing MLB stadium where Jackie Robinson once played.

item.title: Congress Theater Overhaul ‘Full Speed Ahead,’ With Construction To Start In March, Ald. Says
item.description: After a series of funding delays, the revival of the century-old theater could be complete by December 2027 and include affordable housing and a community space.

item.title: Englewood Girl Scouts Had To Sell 2,100 Cookie Boxes To Fund Troop — They’re At 20,000 Now
item.description: Soon after Block Club reported on the troop's mission to sell 2,100 boxes so they could remain active, support from readers across the nation poured in. Now, they want to sell a box to someone in every state.

item.title: Chicago Could Have Its 1st Trans Alderperson As Gronkiewicz-Doran Challenges Gardiner
item.description: S Gronkiewicz-Doran is a Jefferson Park lawyer, affordable housing activist and the first candidate to announce their bid against 45th Ward incumbent Ald. Jim Gardiner in the 2027 election.

item.title: North Side Restaurant Week Returns With More Than 60 Restaurants Offering Special Menus
item.description: Seven North Side neighborhoods, including Lincoln Square, North Center and Albany Park, are taking part in the third annual dining event that kicks off Thursday.

item.title: Does Your Lawn Need A Spring Makeover? The Chicago Fire Want To Help
item.description: The soccer team's elite grounds crew is offering one lucky fan a professional lawn "Fire-Up."

item.title: Bronzeville Historic District Vacant Lots To Become Apartments Under Plan Approved By City Council
item.description: The plan calls for 90 apartments, 18 of which will be affordable. It would be completed by December 2027, according to planning documents.

item.title: Chicago Fire Sets Groundbreaking Ceremony Next Week For New Stadium At The 78
item.description: Mayor Brandon Johnson and Ald. Pat Dowell are expected to speak at the March 3 ceremony. The team aims to have the stadium ready by the 2028-29 season.
